newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: ICC Bank says preparing for competitive future.
newsitem.headline: ICC Bank says preparing for competitive future.

text.p: State-owned ICC Bank, which announced a 20 percent rise in half-year pre-tax profits on Tuesday, said it continued to position itself for a more competitive future banking environment.
"Banking had particularly strong growth in lending, international trade services (I.T.S.) and leasing but margins continued to be tight in all markets," ICC said in a results statement.

It said specific provisions for bad and doubtful debts decreased further and loans and advances to customers increased by more than 19 percent to 994.8 million while Treasury's Customer Deposits rose by 28 percent to 796 million punts.
ICC announced pre-tax profits of 7.0 million Irish pounds for the half year ended April 30th, 1997 compared with 5.9 million in the same period last year.
It said strong growth in the Irish economy and a high level of business activity facilitated growth in gross income which rose to 53.5 million Irish pounds from 48.4 million.
ICC said it continued its special focus on the rapidly growing small to medium sized business sector.
"This sector is making an increased contribution to the economy, particularly in manufacturing, tourism and property," ICC said.
